metadata.title: Atezolizumab 1680 mg Monotherapy – 28 day
metadata.indication: Single-agent atezolizumab across the current NCCP 00593 lung and genitourinary indications.
metadata.safety_correction: Cytotoxic ANC and platelet hold thresholds removed; current v10a ICI-specific adverse-event rules encoded.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding includes NCCP 00593 Version 10a. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.

indications.description: Locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after prior chemotherapy.
Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma after prior platinum-containing chemotherapy.
Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma in adults considered cisplatin-ineligible whose tumours have PD-L1 expression ≥5%.
First-line metastatic NSCLC with high PD-L1 expression and no EGFR mutation or ALK-positive disease.
Maintenance treatment of extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer after completion of induction chemotherapy.
Adjuvant treatment after complete resection and platinum-based chemotherapy for high-risk NSCLC with PD-L1 expression ≥50% and no EGFR or ALK alteration.
NSCLC monotherapy, adjuvant NSCLC and ES-SCLC maintenance indications listed in NCCP 00593.
Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma in an NCCP-listed atezolizumab indication.

indication_id.help: Select the NCCP indication being assessed.

active_infection_requiring_therapy.label: Active clinically significant infection requiring therapy

infection_grade.label: Infection grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No infection. Select the anatomical site-specific CTCAE infection term.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Localised infection requiring local treatment only.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Oral or non-invasive systemic antimicrobial treatment indicated.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: IV antimicrobial treatment, invasive intervention or hospital care indicated.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening infection; urgent intervention required.

infection_grade.assessment_guidance: Use the site-specific CTCAE infection term and grade according to local versus systemic treatment, IV antimicrobials, hospitalisation, organ dysfunction and life-threatening consequences.

pneumonitis_grade.label: Immune-mediated pneumonitis / interstitial lung disease grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No pneumonitis.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Symptomatic; medical intervention indicated; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe symptoms; oxygen indicated; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening respiratory compromise; urgent intervention such as ventilatory support required.

pneumonitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess new cough, dyspnoea, oxygen requirement, imaging findings, infection and alternative causes. Immune-related or drug-related pneumonitis requires urgent senior review when symptomatic.

diarrhoea_colitis_grade.label: Immune-mediated diarrhoea / colitis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: Neither diarrhoea nor colitis is present.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Diarrhoea: fewer than 4 stools/day above baseline or mild ostomy-output increase. Colitis: asymptomatic, clinical/diagnostic observations only.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Diarrhoea: 4-6 stools/day above baseline or moderate ostomy-output increase; limits instrumental ADL. Colitis: abdominal pain or mucus/blood in stool.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Diarrhoea: at least 7 stools/day above baseline, incontinence, hospitalisation or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care ADL. Colitis: severe abdominal pain or peritoneal signs.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening diarrhoea or colitis; urgent intervention required.

diarrhoea_colitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess stool frequency above baseline and also assess abdominal pain, mucus/blood in stool and peritoneal signs. Grade diarrhoea and colitis separately using CTCAE v5.0, then enter the higher applicable grade and document which term determines it.

creatinine_ratio_baseline_or_uln.label: Serum creatinine relative to baseline or ULN

tsh_miu_l.label: TSH
tsh_miu_l.help: Interpret with free T4 and symptoms; no universal numeric hold threshold is encoded.

free_t4_pmol_l.label: Free T4
free_t4_pmol_l.help: Interpret with TSH and symptoms; no universal numeric hold threshold is encoded.

cortisol_nmol_l.label: Cortisol
cortisol_nmol_l.help: Interpret according to sampling time, symptoms and local endocrine guidance.

endocrine_status.label: Immune-mediated endocrine status
endocrine_status.help: Use the clinical syndrome and laboratory pattern together.

rash_grade.label: Immune-mediated rash / dermatitis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No rash. Use the most specific CTCAE skin term when a rash is present.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: For maculopapular rash: under 10% body-surface area, with or without symptoms such as itch, burning or tightness.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: For maculopapular rash: 10–30% body-surface area, or rash limiting instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: For maculopapular rash: over 30% body-surface area with moderate/severe symptoms, or limitation of self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Grade 4 is not defined for uncomplicated maculopapular rash; use the appropriate severe cutaneous-reaction term if life-threatening features are present.

rash_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess morphology, body-surface area, symptoms, mucosal involvement, blistering, systemic features and effect on daily activities. Use the specific CTCAE skin term where possible.

rash_grade_2_over_one_week.label: Grade 2 rash lasting more than one week

myocarditis_grade.label: Immune-mediated myocarditis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No myocarditis.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Grade 1 is not defined for CTCAE v5.0 myocarditis.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Symptoms with moderate activity or exertion.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe symptoms at rest or with minimal activity/exertion; intervention indicated; new onset of symptoms.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention such as continuous IV therapy or mechanical haemodynamic support indicated.

myocarditis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess symptoms at rest and with activity, troponin/other biomarkers, ECG, echocardiography or cardiac MRI as appropriate, treatment required and haemodynamic compromise. Suspected immune-mediated myocarditis requires urgent senior review.

myositis_grade.label: Immune-mediated myositis / polymyositis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No myositis.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild muscle pain.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate pain associated with weakness; pain limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Pain associated with severe weakness; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

myositis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess pain, objective weakness, CK and other relevant investigations, swallowing or respiratory involvement, and impact on instrumental versus self-care activities. Suspected immune-mediated myositis requires urgent senior review.

serious_neurological_irae_grade.label: Serious immune-mediated neurological syndrome grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No serious neurological adverse event.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild symptoms under the named CTCAE neurological term.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate symptoms limiting instrumental activities of daily living under the named term.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe symptoms limiting self-care activities of daily living or requiring hospital care under the named term.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening neurological consequences; urgent intervention required.

serious_neurological_irae_grade.help: For syndromes such as myasthenia gravis, encephalitis, Guillain–Barré syndrome, myelitis or meningitis.
serious_neurological_irae_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify and document the exact neurological adverse event before grading. Assess objective deficit, instrumental versus self-care ADL limitation, bulbar/respiratory involvement and need for hospitalisation.

infusion_reaction_grade.label: Infusion-related reaction grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No infusion-related or hypersensitivity reaction.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild transient reaction; interruption of the infusion is not indicated; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Infusion interruption or treatment is indicated, with prompt response to symptomatic medication; prophylaxis may be needed for 24 hours or less.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Prolonged symptoms not rapidly responsive to treatment/brief interruption, or recurrence after initial improvement; hospitalisation indicated for clinical sequelae.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

infusion_reaction_grade.assessment_guidance: Document timing, symptoms, need to interrupt treatment, response to symptomatic therapy, recurrence, hospitalisation and any airway or haemodynamic compromise.

other_immune_toxicity_grade.label: Other immune-mediated toxicity grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No adverse event.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild or asymptomatic; clinical observation only and intervention generally not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate; minimal, local or non-invasive intervention may be indicated; may limit instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe or medically significant but not immediately life-threatening; hospital care may be indicated; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

other_immune_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify the actual adverse event first, then apply that toxicity-specific CTCAE definition. The generic severity anchors are not a substitute for the named CTCAE criterion.

other_nonimmune_toxicity_grade.label: Other non-immune adverse reaction grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No adverse event.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild or asymptomatic; clinical observation only and intervention generally not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate; minimal, local or non-invasive intervention may be indicated; may limit instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe or medically significant but not immediately life-threatening; hospital care may be indicated; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

other_nonimmune_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify the actual adverse event first, then apply that toxicity-specific CTCAE definition. The generic severity anchors are not a substitute for the named CTCAE criterion.

fbc_clinical_concern.label: FBC abnormality requiring clinical review
fbc_clinical_concern.help: FBC abnormalities are monitored but do not trigger a protocol-defined ANC/platelet hold unless the source protocol states a threshold.

pancreatitis_grade.label: Immune-mediated pancreatitis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No pancreatitis.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Grade 1 is not defined for CTCAE pancreatitis.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Enzyme elevation or imaging findings only, without significant symptoms.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe pain or vomiting requiring medical intervention.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

pancreatitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess symptoms, pancreatic enzymes, imaging, oral intake, IV fluid/analgesia requirements, hospitalisation and organ dysfunction.

pericardial_disorder_grade.label: Immune-mediated pericardial disorder grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No pericardial adverse event. Use the named CTCAE pericardial term.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: For pericarditis: asymptomatic ECG or physical findings consistent with pericarditis. Pericardial effusion has no Grade 1 criterion.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Symptomatic pericarditis (for example chest pain), or asymptomatic small-to-moderate pericardial effusion.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Pericarditis or effusion with physiological consequences, such as constriction or clinically significant haemodynamic effects.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences, including tamponade physiology; urgent intervention required.

pericardial_disorder_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess symptoms, ECG/echo findings, effusion or tamponade physiology, treatment required and haemodynamic compromise.

ketones_mmol_l.label: Blood ketones (optional if hyperglycaemia or symptoms)

action.recommendation: Do not administer atezolizumab; obtain consultant review.

rules.explanation: Relevant hypersensitivity is an exclusion.

action.recommendation: Do not proceed without urgent consultant review of pregnancy or breastfeeding risk.

rules.explanation: Pregnancy or breastfeeding requires specialist review.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab and treat/review the infection until clinically stable.

rules.explanation: Clinically significant active infection requires review before treatment.

action.recommendation: Review the FBC abnormality clinically; no protocol-defined ANC or platelet hold threshold is encoded for single-agent atezolizumab.

rules.explanation: FBC is monitored, but NCCP 00593 does not specify an ANC or platelet treatment threshold.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab and manage as immune-mediated pneumonitis.

rules.explanation: Grade 2 pneumonitis requires withholding.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for grade 3–4 pneumonitis.

rules.explanation: Grade 3–4 pneumonitis requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab and manage as immune-mediated hepatitis.

rules.explanation: ALT/AST >3–5×ULN or bilirubin >1.5–3×ULN requires withholding.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for severe immune-mediated hepatitis.

rules.explanation: ALT/AST >5×ULN or bilirubin >3×ULN requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab and manage the immune-mediated diarrhoea/colitis pathway.

rules.explanation: Grade 2–3 immune-mediated diarrhoea/colitis requires withholding.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for grade 4 diarrhoea/colitis.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 diarrhoea/colitis requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab until symptomatic thyroid dysfunction is controlled and thyroid function is improving.

rules.explanation: Symptomatic hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism requires withholding.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab until clinically stable on appropriate replacement therapy.

rules.explanation: Symptomatic adrenal insufficiency or grade 2–3 hypophysitis requires withholding.

action.recommendation: Controlled endocrinopathy on replacement therapy does not automatically require permanent discontinuation; confirm stability.

rules.explanation: Controlled endocrinopathies are an exception to the general permanent-discontinuation rule.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab and urgently establish metabolic control with insulin.

rules.explanation: Suspected immune-mediated diabetes with glucose >13.9 mmol/L meets the grade 3–4 hyperglycaemia pathway.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab and refer for specialist assessment of suspected SCAR.

rules.explanation: Suspected SJS/TEN or another SCAR requires withholding.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for confirmed SJS/TEN or another severe cutaneous adverse reaction.

rules.explanation: Confirmed SJS/TEN requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab for grade 3 immune-mediated rash.

rules.explanation: Grade 3 rash requires withholding.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for grade 4 rash.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 rash requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab and manage the immune-mediated pancreatitis pathway.

rules.explanation: Grade 2–3 pancreatitis or amylase/lipase >2×ULN with grade 3–4 elevation requires withholding.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for grade 4 or recurrent pancreatitis.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 pancreatitis requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab and urgently manage suspected immune-mediated myocarditis.

rules.explanation: Grade 2 or above myocarditis requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab and manage as immune-mediated nephritis.

rules.explanation: Creatinine >1.5–3× baseline or ULN meets the grade 2 nephritis pathway.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for grade 3–4 nephritis.

rules.explanation: Creatinine >3× baseline or ULN requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab and manage immune-mediated myositis.

rules.explanation: Grade 2–3 myositis requires withholding.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for grade 4 or recurrent grade 3 myositis.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 or recurrent grade 3 myositis requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab and urgently manage the serious neurological immune-mediated syndrome.

rules.explanation: Serious neurological immune-mediated syndromes generally require permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab and obtain detailed cardiac assessment.

rules.explanation: Grade 1 pericardial disorder requires withholding and cardiac evaluation.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for grade 2 or higher pericardial disorder.

rules.explanation: Grade 2 or higher pericardial disorder requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab and urgently assess/manage suspected HLH.

rules.explanation: Suspected haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Withhold atezolizumab until recovery to grade 0–1 and steroid reduction as specified.

rules.explanation: Grade 2–3 other immune-mediated toxicity requires withholding.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for grade 4 immune-mediated toxicity, except controlled endocrinopathies.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 other immune-mediated toxicity requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for recurrent grade 3 immune-mediated toxicity.

rules.explanation: Recurrent grade 3 immune-mediated toxicity requires permanent discontinuation.

action.recommendation: Reduce the infusion rate or interrupt; treatment may resume once the event resolves.

rules.explanation: Grade 1–2 infusion reactions require slowing or interruption.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue atezolizumab for a grade 3–4 infusion reaction.

rules.explanation: Grade 3–4 infusion reactions require permanent discontinuation.

output_templates.proceed: No encoded immune-toxicity or exclusion rule was triggered. Complete normal prescribing, laboratory, clinical and pharmacy checks.
output_templates.coverage_gap: One or more potentially relevant ICI domains were not assessed.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Highest active parenteral component is minimal emetogenic risk in NCCP V6 Table 7.
